statements.impact_statement: golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained and flagged unsafe by design regardless of usage. govulncheck's reported call chain shows Zarf's signing path (src/pkg/signing/cosign.go CosignSignBlobWithOptions -> cosign's SignBlobCmd -> sigstore-go pkg/sign.Bundle/GetTransparencyLogEntry) reaching rekor's PGP public-key parser (pkg/pki/pgp.NewPublicKey -> golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp ReadKeyRing/ReadEntity/addUserID/VerifyUserIdSignature). This is a static-analysis over-approximation: rekor's pki.NewArtifactFactory dispatches to one PKI implementation via an explicit Format argument (pkg/pki/factory.go), and sigstore-go hardcodes that format to x509 for every hashedrekord transparency-log entry it creates (pkg/sign/transparency.go: artifactProperties.PKIFormat = string(pki.X509)). Zarf never supplies or accepts PGP-format keys in its signing flags, so the PGP branch of rekor's format dispatch, and therefore the vulnerable openpgp code, is never exercised at runtime.
